title: Scale Helm: compact fleet throughput controls, policy simulator & event timeline
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Ship a compact, operator-focused Fleet Controls panel that combines three tightly integrated capabilities: 1) a compact scaling control ("Slider + quick presets + advanced threshold editor") + 2) a throughput & latency dashboard oriented around tenant-level heatmaps and p99 token throughput trends, and 3) an immutable event timeline for scaling changes with annotations and one-click rollback to a previous policy.

Why: Customers running Dedicated need a single surface to make fast, low-risk scaling decisions during spikes or incident windows. Existing consoles spread controls and history across multiple screens, forcing context switches and manual reconciliation. This ticket consolidates operator flows and adds a lightweight policy simulator so teams can preview the unit-cost and latency impact before applying changes.

Non-goals: This work does not replace the full Capacity Planner (forecast engine) or the autoscaler tuning service. We will not implement cross-region failover controls in this iteration.

Design references: mockups and flow: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/scale-helm-mocks (v3). Specs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Scale+Helm+Compact+Controls.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Implementation notes: Frontend will add a 'Scale Helm' panel within Fleet > Controls. Backend APIs required: GET /fleet/{id}/scaling-policy (existing, extend to return policy metadata), POST /fleet/{id}/policy-simulate (new, lightweight simulation returning cost and latency delta estimates), PATCH /fleet/{id}/apply-policy (uses existing rollout engine). We'll create an appendix doc for API contracts and telemetry metrics (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8142).

Rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged beta to internal SRE and two pilot customers (2 weeks), 2) collect telemetry and iterate (1 sprint), 3) wide release behind RBAC control.

Safety & rollback: all apply operations will continue to create an immutable event in the event timeline with a generated policy snapshot id. Rollback uses that snapshot id via POST /fleet/{id}/rollback-policy.

Operational metrics to capture: event create rate, simulator usage rate, apply error rate, time-to-first-stable (operator applies change until 95th percentile latency returns to baseline).
acceptance_criteria: Compact scaling control visible in Fleet > Controls for fleets with Dedicated capacity
Policy simulator compiles and returns cost and latency delta estimates within 300ms median for typical policy diffs
Throughput dashboard shows per-tenant token/sec heatmap, 1h/6h/24h aggregations, and p99 latency overlay
Event timeline records every policy apply/rollback with who/when/why metadata and links to the associated rollout (immutable)
Operators can rollback to any previous policy snapshot from the timeline and the rollback action is audited
Telemetry emitted for simulator use, apply success/fail, and rollback events (instrumentation PR merged)
UI is behind feature flag and gated by RBAC role 'fleet-operator'
